subject: Performance safeguard + annual true-up proposal for multi-year prepay
messages:
From: Tom Harrison <tom.harrison@brightlayer.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlayer.com, Elena Santos <elena.santos@brightlayer.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Multi-year prepay — performance safeguard and true-up

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. BrightLayer is very interested in a 2–3 year committed prepay but we need two items to get internal approval: a performance safeguard (SLA credit or rebate if inference latency exceeds the agreed SLO for consecutive weeks) and a clear annual true-up mechanism so our finance team can reconcile usage vs committed spend.

High-level ask:
- 2-year commitment with annual true-up (adjust downwards if usage materially under-indexes)
- Performance safeguard tied to 99th-percentile token latency per region (proposal: credit of X% of monthly invoice for sustained misses)
- Prefer pricing and examples in Excel so we can run scenarios with our FP&A team

Can you put together language and a pricing example? I can loop legal/procurement after we have a draft.

Thanks,
Tom Harrison
Head of Cloud Ops — BrightLayer

--
Attachment: BrightLayer_RFP_notes.txt (text)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>
To: Tom Harrison <tom.harrison@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay — performance safeguard and true-up

Tom —

Appreciate the clarity. I attached a short SOW + an Excel workbook with two pricing scenarios: 2-year and 3-year prepay. The workbook includes an illustrative true-up line (annual reconciliation with a 30-day settlement window) and two safeguard options: credit vs invoice or a rebate payable at true-up.

Attachments: BrightLayer_MultiYear_SOW.pdf, proposed_pricing.xlsx

A couple of notes up front:
- We generally prefer to handle performance as an SLA credit (applied in month following validated misses) rather than cash rebates; credits preserve committed pathway for both teams.
- For multi-year rates we can grant stepped discount bands tied to committed dollars and escalating usage tiers. If you want a floor (minimum monthly ramp) we can include a phased ramp schedule.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the workbook and pick the guardrails you prefer? I can bring Ben and Neha.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>, Tom Harrison <tom.harrison@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay — performance safeguard and true-up

Tom / Rafael —

Quick context from a sales perspective: we can be flexible with total discount if BrightLayer accepts a limited warranty-style performance safeguard (not open-ended cash refunds). Suggested structure:
- 2-year: up to 18% blended discount on list for a ballast commit with annual true-up
- 3-year: up to 22% blended discount if you commit to a 12-month minimum ramp schedule (phased floor)

On safeguards: recommend SLA credit per incident window with severity buckets (e.g., sustained 99p misses over 2 weeks -> 5% credit; over 4 weeks -> 12% credit). Rebate payable only in lieu of credits and at true-up to avoid monthly cash flow complexity.

I'll be on the call. Rafael — please flag any non-negotiables from our procurement playbook.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Tom Harrison <tom.harrison@brightlayer.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay — performance safeguard and true-up

Tom — Rafael —

Finance perspective: we can approve an 18% effective discount for a 24-month prepay under these conditions:
1) Annual true-up with a 30-day settlement window; underage is credited against next invoice or cash-settled at mutual option.
2) Performance safeguard implemented as SLA credits applied monthly; if cumulative credits exceed 10% of annual committed spend we escalate to a one-time rebate at true-up (rebate memo attached with formula examples).
3) Phased ramp: months 1–3 = 40% of expected monthly run-rate, months 4–12 target 80–100% depending on onboarding milestones. Failure to meet ramp can trigger re-pricing on the remaining term at a predetermined interpolation.

Attached: rebate_memo.pdf (formula and worked examples). We will need a short exhibit in the SOW that codifies the credit and rebate triggers. Also please add a single line item describing the audit/usage sample window (FP&A and Redwood will reconcile usage logs).

- Neha Kapoor
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Tom Harrison <tom.harrison@brightlayer.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay — performance safeguard and true-up

Tom —

Thanks for outlining the asks. After reviewing the SOW and the finance memo, I’m comfortable approving a conditional 18% discount for a 24-month prepay with the following guardrails:
- SLA credit-first approach; rebate only if cumulative annual credits exceed 10% of committed spend (paid at annual true-up).
- 30-day true-up settlement window and a predefined phased ramp schedule as Neha described.
- Add an agreed dispute timeline (45 days) and the ability for either party to request a usage audit with mutually agreed logs.

Rafael — please have Legal draft a brief exhibit capturing credit triggers and the true-up flow (we prefer simple math tables and example months). Also attach redline instructions for BrightLayer to comment. I’ve asked Legal to prioritize this but we’ll need procurement looped once BrightLayer confirms the workbook scenario.

Tom — if that aligns with BrightLayer’s needs, Rafael will send the redline-ready SOW and the DocuSign starter link (below) and we can move to procurement.

DocuSign starter: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=abc123-brightlayer
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/BL-2026-0912

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redline_instructions.txt (short list of clause IDs we expect comments on)
